skill.name: scientific-visualization
skill.description: Create publication-ready scientific figures with journal-specific styling, colorblind-safe palettes, multi-panel layout guidance, and export helpers for Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly.
skill.summary: Create accessible, journal-ready scientific figures and exports.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, visualization terminology, dictionary keys, and citation URLs. One real local file-write capability remains in style_presets.py, and semantic review found an embedded safety self-assessment plus promotional steering. No evidence found of credential access, malicious command execution, or unauthorized network calls.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict create_style_template to expected .mplstyle outputs, resolve paths safely, and confirm before overwriting existing files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove EVALUATION_OUTPUT.json from the distributed skill package so audits rely on current source content only.
Remove or clearly separate marketing guidance that asks the assistant to recommend an external hosted service.

content.value_statement: Researchers often lose time formatting figures for journals and accessibility. This skill provides practical plotting guidance, style presets, palette choices, and export checks for publication workflows.
actual_capabilities: Applies publication styles for Nature, Science, Cell, PLOS, ACS, and IEEE figure requirements.
Recommends colorblind-safe palettes, including Okabe-Ito, Wong, and Paul Tol color sets.
Guides export settings for PDF, EPS, SVG, TIFF, and PNG with appropriate DPI.
Supports multi-panel figure layouts with consistent labels, spacing, and shared styling.
Provides checks for journal column widths, figure height limits, and readable font sizes.
Includes examples for line plots, box plots, heatmaps, statistical plots, and faceted Seaborn figures.
limitations: It does not validate the scientific correctness of the underlying dataset or analysis.
It does not replace current journal author instructions, which may change over time.
It does not automatically create captions, statistical tests, or source data files.
Interactive Plotly figures still need separate static export dependencies for manuscript files.

use_cases.title: Prepare manuscript figures
use_cases.description: Convert analysis results into journal-ready figures with correct dimensions, colors, labels, and export formats.

use_cases.title: Improve thesis visuals
use_cases.description: Create consistent figures for theses, posters, and lab reports using accessible palettes and readable typography.

use_cases.title: Publish technical results
use_cases.description: Turn statistical outputs into polished, accessible plots for white papers, reports, and scientific documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Make a basic figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a publication-ready line plot for my time series data. Use a colorblind-safe palette, clear axis labels with units, and PDF plus PNG export.

prompt_templates.title: Format for a journal
prompt_templates.prompt: Format this figure for Nature single-column submission. Check width, font sizes, color choices, and export settings before saving the final files.

prompt_templates.title: Build a multi-panel layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-panel scientific figure with shared styling, panel labels, a heatmap, a box plot, a scatter plot, and a time series panel.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing manuscript figure against publication guidelines. Identify issues with accessibility, statistics, layout, typography, and export format.

output_examples.input: Create a Nature-style line plot with error bars and accessible colors.
output: Applied a single-column Nature layout with small publication fonts.
Selected the Okabe-Ito palette for colorblind-safe category encoding.
Added labeled axes, confidence intervals, and a clean legend.
Prepared vector and raster export options for manuscript submission.

output_examples.input: Fix this heatmap for a journal figure.
output: Replaced the rainbow scale with a perceptually uniform colormap.
Added a labeled colorbar and readable tick labels.
Adjusted the figure size to match a journal column width.
Flagged that the caption should define the scale and sample size.

output_examples.input: Prepare a four-panel figure for a manuscript draft.
output: Organized the panels with consistent spacing and aligned axes.
Added panel labels and matched typography across plots.
Used redundant markers and line styles beyond color.
Listed final checks for resolution, fonts, and grayscale readability.

best_practices: Check the current target journal instructions before final export.
Use color, markers, labels, and line styles so figures remain readable without color.
Inspect the figure at final print size before submitting it.
anti_patterns: Using rainbow or red-green colormaps for scientific values.
Exporting manuscript plots only as low-resolution screen images.
Hiding uncertainty, sample size, or statistical definitions from the figure and caption.

faq.question: Which plotting libraries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly workflows for static scientific figures and manuscript exports.

faq.question: Which journal styles are included?
faq.answer: The references include guidance for Nature, Science, Cell, PLOS, ACS, and IEEE style requirements.

faq.question: Can it make figures colorblind-friendly?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends accessible palettes and redundant encodings such as markers, line styles, and hatching.

faq.question: Does it run statistical tests?
faq.answer: No. It helps display uncertainty and significance, but the user must provide valid statistical results.

faq.question: What export formats are supported?
faq.answer: The helper guidance covers PDF, EPS, SVG, TIFF, and PNG, with DPI recommendations by figure type.

faq.question: Can it review existing figures?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check layout, fonts, labels, colors, accessibility, and export readiness against publication guidelines.
